 Director of K-Pop Demon Hunters: Don't try to explain the culture, tell your own story.
 VTV.vn - Once feeling insecure about being Korean while growing up in Toronto, Canada, Maggie Kang has now achieved global fame with "KPop Demon Hunters".
 Đài truyền hình Việt Nam • 25/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Photo: Netflix
 At CNN's Global Perspectives forum in Bangkok, Thailand , the director shared how she transformed childhood traumas into inspiration for her work. Her story also raises a thought-provoking question: does an artist need to represent their entire culture, or simply be true to what they genuinely want to tell?
 A pillar of identity 
 Growing up in Toronto, Maggie Kang felt out of place even among her Asian friends. When her Chinese friends celebrated Lunar New Year according to their own traditions, she realized she didn't truly belong, but she also hadn't found a deep enough connection to her Korean roots. "I felt like an inferior Asian, and that was sad," Kang recalled.
 Nevertheless, the multicultural environment in Toronto also gave her the opportunity to explore her own identity. Her parents often told Kang about Korean history, helping her understand the journey of a small nation situated between powerful countries like Japan and China. Understanding her national history helped Kang view her roots from a different perspective. She gradually found pride in the stories of her country. 
 Director Maggie Kang attends the Global Viewpoint program in Bangkok, Thailand (Photo: screenshot)
 This shift is taking place against the backdrop of Korean culture's growing international influence. The success of film and television, particularly the Oscar-winning film Parasite , along with the strong growth of K-pop, has brought Korean stories and artists closer to global audiences.
 You may also like Maggie Kang recalls the surprise of witnessing a culture she once thought was undervalued become a prominent part of popular culture. She noticed that while Koreans were involved in producing many animated projects for other markets, their own unique works hadn't truly become widespread. She wanted to contribute to changing that with a film that explored Korean culture in its own way. However, that idea took years to realize. Maggie Kang spent over a decade building relationships within the industry, working with producers and studios, and proving her capabilities before being given the opportunity to direct her first film. 
 The portrayal of Kpop female fans in the film is a reflection of Maggie Kang's own teenage story (Photo: Netflix).
 She expressed her gratitude to Netflix Animation for allowing her to take on multiple roles in the creative process, from directing and writing the script to contributing to the music . In particular, the studio supported her determination to use an all-Korean main cast.
 Be honest with yourself. 
 When embarking on KPop Demon Hunters , Maggie Kang realized that telling a story rooted in her heritage also meant facing high expectations. While never doubting her own identity, she worried about whether she had enough understanding of Korean culture to convincingly incorporate it into the film. Her father's advice helped alleviate these concerns. "You can only make a film that reflects yourself," Kang recalled her father saying. "Remove the cultural elements from it. It should all revolve around you and what you want to do."
 That advice helped her realize something: even her older sister, who grew up in the same family, had a different perspective on Korean culture than she did. "Therefore, I don't need to represent everyone; I just need to be honest with my own point of view." When creating her female characters, Maggie Kang thought of herself as a child. As a K-pop fan, she used to dream of seeing female characters on screen who resembled her favorites. But back then, she rarely found such characters. 
 Director Maggie Kang believes that to make a compelling film, you need to start with what you want to tell the story. (Image: screenshot)
 You may also like Maggie Kang once told people in the film industry that she was willing to participate in projects about Korean culture and K-pop girls. However, the right opportunity didn't come along. So she decided to make the film she had always wanted to see herself. This choice wasn't without risk. Maggie Kang told her husband that if the film wasn't well-received, she might not make films anymore, because her debut work contained so much about herself. "The compliments that touched me the most weren't about the scale or success of the film, but when friends said they saw me on screen."
 Director Maggie Kang confirmed that a sequel to the Kpop film Demon Hunter is in development but did not reveal details. She expressed her desire to collaborate with more international artists and to learn more about the music of other countries.
